text:
Utah took the points in Toronto the way a better team usually does, by piling up quality chances until one of them counted. Nick Schmaltz's backhand on a third-period power play, a 78% look by our numbers, broke a 2-2 tie and sent UTA home with a 3-2 win. It also evened the season series, after the Mammoth won 5-4 in the first meeting on Oct. 13.

The scoreboard undersold the gap. UTA generated 4.12 expected goals (a measure of chance quality, where every shot is graded by how often it scores) to TOR's 1.72, and our simulation says UTA deserved to win 87% of the time, meaning it takes that share of simulated replays of every shot. Clayton Keller was the engine, with three assists and a line that controlled the ice: UTA's chances with him out there outran TOR's 2.17 to 0.28. Mikhail Sergachev, drafted ninth overall by Montreal out of Windsor in 2016, added two assists in nearly 26 minutes. Sergei Bobrovsky kept it close, stopping 1.1 more goals than the shots against him deserved.

TOR stayed in it with two goals from Jack Roslovic, who was a 25th overall pick by Winnipeg in 2015. The second tied the game midway through the third on a backhand, set up by Auston Matthews and Morgan Rielly. But the Maple Leafs went 0 for 2 on the power play while UTA converted two of three. UTA leaves Toronto with the win and the series split, while TOR drops the rematch despite the best efforts of its goalie.
